- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience.
- Model often lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days; apply a 1-day forward bias in forecasts if sentiment is trending.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; dampen forecast slope for 2–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; align forecast toward recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates true volatility in high-sentiment periods; increase forecast variance or add 2–3% upward buffer.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model fails to anticipate direction change; add 1–2 day lag correction.
